title: Surjit Bhalla: SIR needs reform. But let’s go by numbers, not protestors’ slogans
shows: It replies to Jean Drèze and Yogendra Yadav. For the nine states with final rolls, it takes the figures of 59.9 crore adults and 52.8 crore names, allows for 5.2 crore young people who were not registered in 2024 and 1.5% of adults for older people who never registered, and puts the eligible people wrongly left off at about 1 crore. It also lists what the Commission has not published, including a national roll after the revision and deletions by reason, state and booth.
quote: A crore of eligible voters wrongly removed is not nothing.

title: Karnataka’s most backward districts see low applications for inclusion after SIR draft deletions
shows: The paper sets district figures from Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer for Kalaburagi, Mysuru, Raichur and Ballari, where more than 18% of the electorate was left off the draft roll, against the Form 6 applications received by 23 September. Mysuru received 35,447 against more than 5.57 lakh left off. The office has not released the age of applicants, so first-time voters cannot be told apart from those seeking to return.
quote: The applications remain disproportionately low compared with the scale of deletions.

title: 90% of 33 lakh SIR cases ‘resolved’ or ‘parked for final roll’ in Delhi
shows: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office said on 23 October that about 29.5 lakh of the nearly 33 lakh notice cases, 13.79 lakh unmapped and 19.33 lakh flagged for logical discrepancies, had been resolved or parked for the final roll. It did not say how many were rejected. The report also gives the Form 6 count since the draft roll, 2,50,754, and Maharashtra's proposal to change Form 6 for voters seeking to return.
quote: The CEO’s office did not disclose how many cases had been rejected.
